findings.title: ADR-0005 decisions 12 and 14 describe a Project signature and rejection codes the code does not have
findings.summary: ADR-0005 decision 12 says `Decision.Project(bool unknownAs)` ("the parameter is a bool so an Unknown replacement cannot be requested") and decisions 12/14 say a rule that spells Project/Collapse is rejected with SyntaxError TRE0001 (DSL) or MalformedTree TRE0014 (JSON/YAML). The code has `Project(TruthValue unknownAs)` that throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException at runtime for Unknown (src/TruthWeaver.Abstractions/Decision.cs:82-88), and every surface rejects Project/Collapse with UnknownPredicate TRE0002 (src/TruthWeaver/Parsing/DslParser.cs:1083,1115; CollapseRejection.cs:20). CONTEXT.md, docs/strong-k3/result-transformations/project.md:11,48 and specification/diagnostics.md:16 agree with the code, so the ADR text is the stale side.
findings.failure_scenario: A reader who trusts the ADR (declared ground truth) writes `decision.Project(true)` and gets a compile error, or filters diagnostics on TRE0001/TRE0014 to catch a persisted `Collapse(...)` rule and never sees it because the engine emits TRE0002. Expected: the ADR and the code name the same signature and code.
findings.expected_behavior: ADR-0005 decisions 12 and 14 are amended in place to `Project(TruthValue unknownAs)` (Unknown rejected with ArgumentOutOfRangeException) and to UnknownPredicate (TRE0002) on every surface, matching the code and the reference pages.

findings.title: ADR-0005 says JSON/YAML do not read the constant letters, but the parsers, schema and reference docs do
findings.summary: Decision 16 states "JSON and YAML do not read the letters" (T/F/U) and decision 13 still gives the Unknown literal as `{"op": "unknown"}`. The code accepts the letters in both tree formats (src/TruthWeaver/Json/JsonNodeCursor.cs:112, src/TruthWeaver.Yaml/YamlNodeCursor.cs:112), rule-tree.schema.json:61-69 allows them, and docs/rule-formats.md:74 and docs/strong-k3/specification/syntax.md:16 document `{"const": "U"}` / `const: U`. The Unknown literal is `{"const": "unknown"}`, not an `op`. The ADR is the stale side.
findings.failure_scenario: A tool author follows the ADR and writes a validator that rejects `{"const": "U"}` or expects `{"op": "unknown"}`; the engine compiles the first and rejects the second (`unknown` is not an operator: TRE0002). Expected: one documented set of accepted spellings.
findings.expected_behavior: Amend decision 16 to say the tree formats read the letters, and strike or amend decision 13's `{"op": "unknown"}` example to `{"const": "unknown"}`.

findings.title: The `const` diagnostic lists fewer spellings than the parser accepts
findings.summary: JSON and YAML accept `true`/`false`/`unknown` in any case and the letters T/F/U (TryGetTruthValue at lines 98-117; YamlNodeCursor.cs:107-113), but the TRE0014 message and Expected text say only "a JSON boolean or one of \"true\", \"false\", \"unknown\"" (JsonNodeCursor.cs:24-25, YamlNodeCursor.cs:24-25). The rule-formats page and the schema say the letters are valid.
findings.failure_scenario: Input `{"const": "unk"}` gives: "'const' must be a JSON boolean or one of \"true\", \"false\", \"unknown\"." A user who then writes `{"const": "U"}` because the docs say so is left unsure whether the diagnostic or the docs is right. Expected: the diagnostic names every accepted spelling.
findings.expected_behavior: The ConstMessage/ConstExpected vocabulary names the three words and the three letters (case-insensitive), matching docs/rule-formats.md:74.

findings.title: "could not be evaluated" (faulted) and "not evaluated" (skipped) are near-identical words for different states
findings.summary: `Explain` phrases a faulted term as "could not be evaluated" (DecisionExplainer.cs:75-78; TraceReasons.cs:65 says the same), while the trace, the decision record and the debugger views use "not evaluated" / `notEvaluated` for a term that short-circuiting skipped (TraceEntry.cs:24, TraceNode.cs:36, TraceReasons.cs:7, docs/decision-records.md:173). ADR-0002 and the glossary define NotEvaluated as skipped only. A faulted term is `notEvaluated: false` in the same record.
findings.failure_scenario: Rule `isOff AND boom` evaluated in ShortCircuit mode: the record shows `boom` with `notEvaluated: true` (skipped). The same rule in Exhaustive mode, with `boom` throwing: `Explain` returns "Not satisfied." for the False result but for `boom OR isOff` returns "Unknown because boom could not be evaluated" while the record shows `notEvaluated: false`. A support reader searching logs for "not evaluated" conflates skipped and faulted terms.
findings.expected_behavior: One word per state: faulted terms say "faulted" (the project term in CONTEXT.md), and "not evaluated" is reserved for short-circuit skips.

findings.title: docs/data-sources.md names `UnsupportedType` as a fault kind for JSON null, but the recorded fault kind is TypeMismatch
findings.summary: The "Missing, null and empty values" table says a JSON `null`/object/array match records a fault of kind "`TypeMismatch`, or `UnsupportedType` for `null`". `VariableFailureKind` has no `UnsupportedType` member (src/TruthWeaver.Abstractions/VariableFailureKind.cs); JsonDataSource reports `DataQueryErrorKind.UnsupportedType` for null (JsonDataSource.cs:161,172) and the evaluator maps it to `VariableFailureKind.TypeMismatch` for every node kind (src/TruthWeaver/Evaluation/Evaluator.cs:801-804). The behaviour (Unknown plus a fault, never False or an exception) is right; the doc names the wrong kind. The doc side is wrong.
findings.failure_scenario: A host filters `Decision.Faults` for `VariableResolutionException.Kind == UnsupportedType` to count null data, as the table suggests; the code does not compile, or a switch on `Kind` never sees the null case because it arrives as `TypeMismatch`.
findings.expected_behavior: The row says the fault kind is `TypeMismatch` for a null, object or array match, with the source's `UnsupportedType` only in the message.

findings.title: A data source that answers QueryAsync with NoMatch or AmbiguousMatch is reported as a source error, not missing/ambiguous
findings.summary: `QuerySourceUncachedAsync` maps every `DataQueryErrorKind` other than `UnsupportedType` to `VariableFailureKind.SourceError` (Evaluator.cs:801-807), so a custom `IDataSource` that returns `DataQueryResult.Failure(DataQueryErrorKind.NoMatch, ...)` or `AmbiguousMatch` from `QueryAsync` (the API accepts any kind) gets the trace word "source error" and a `SourceError` fault instead of "missing"/"ambiguous". The enum doc (DataQueryErrorKind.cs:15-19) says those two kinds are for `ScopeAsync`, but nothing in `DataQueryResult.Failure` enforces it and docs/data-sources.md "Writing your own data source" does not say to return `Empty()` for no match.
findings.failure_scenario: A host writes a database-backed source that returns `Failure(NoMatch, "no row")` when a scalar query finds nothing. The trace reads `[from("db", "$.x"): source error]` and `Fault.Exception.Kind` is `SourceError`; an operator triages it as an outage rather than missing data, which is the documented `Missing` outcome for the same situation in the JSON source.
findings.expected_behavior: Either map `NoMatch` to `Missing` and `AmbiguousMatch` to `Ambiguous`, or document in `DataQueryResult.Failure` and the data-sources guide that a query source must answer no match with `Empty()` and that those two kinds are scope-only.

findings.title: YAML `const:` with an empty or `~` value reports Found as a quoted empty string rather than null
findings.summary: `DescribeValue` quotes the scalar text whenever the node is a scalar (`node is YamlScalarNode { Value: { } text } ? $"'{text}'"`), so an empty or `~` value is described as `''` or `'~'`, while `Describe` (line 65) and the argument-literal path treat the same scalar as `null`. TreeFormatReader uses DescribeValue for a bad `const` (TreeFormatReader.cs:224).
findings.failure_scenario: YAML `const:` (no value) gives TRE0014 with Found `''`. A user does not see that the engine read a null; the JSON equivalent `{"const": null}` reports Found `null`.
findings.expected_behavior: DescribeValue returns "null" for a YAML null scalar, as Describe does, so JSON and YAML report the same thing for the same mistake.
